articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a record-breaking 200 patches in one Patch Tuesday cycle, including 36 critical vulns. Either they've been hoarding fixes or the code quality is reaching new depths of despair.

articles.title: Victory! 702 has Expired!
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally yeeted AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets to GitHub, prompting congressional demands for answers. When the cybersecurity watchdog can't watch its own data, who watches the watchers?

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: Section 702 surveillance authority finally expires after years of constitutional violations disguised as foreign intelligence gathering. One small step for privacy, one giant leap away from the surveillance state.

articles.title: Claude Fable 5 Doesn't Change the Mythos Security Story
articles.summary: ShinyHunters exploits Oracle ERP zero-day to ransack American universities' data like it's 2012 again. Higher education gets a brutal lesson in why legacy enterprise software is a security nightmare.

articles.title: U.S. Orders Anthropic to Suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 Access for Foreign Nationals
articles.summary: Critical Splunk Enterprise flaw scores 9.8 CVSS, allowing unauthenticated RCE because apparently enterprise logging platforms are now attack vectors. The irony of security tools being insecure never gets old.

articles.title: Google Sues Chinese Smishing Network Accused of Using Gemini AI in Phishing
articles.summary: Over 400 Arch Linux AUR packages hijacked to deploy credential stealers and eBPF rootkits. Supply chain attacks hit the DIY Linux crowd where it hurts: their beloved user repository.

articles.title: US government orders Anthropic to kill Fable 5 and Mythos 5 in unprecedented AI model recall
articles.summary: China-linked Velvet Ant crew backdoored Linux PAM and OpenSSH for nearly a decade, hiding in plain sight in the login system itself. Sometimes the best place to hide is where everyone looks but no one sees.

articles.title: The new BitLocker exploit everyone's freaking out about probably won't affect you
articles.summary: Autonomous security agent discovers 21 zero-days in FFmpeg after Google and Anthropic's analysis missed them all. AI finds what humans couldn't, proving that even the robots are better at breaking things than we are.

articles.title: Oracle Addresses PeopleSoft Vulnerability Amid Reports of Zero-Day Attacks
articles.summary: Oracle warns of security flaw actively exploited by cybercrime gangs in mass-hacking campaign affecting 100+ organizations. Classic Oracle: patch late, communicate poorly, leave customers exposed.

articles.title: Oracle warns of security bug that hackers abused to breach 100+ companies | TechCrunch
articles.summary: 23andMe settles 2023 data breach for $46.75M after exposing users' genetic data and ancestry information. Your DNA is worth about $47 million in settlement money, apparently.
